name: Orbit AI - CRM Architecture - Location Contract Lock check (05 Section 13, new - not brief-W-numbered)

nodes.name: Location lock check webhook
nodes.notes: 05 Section 13: 'each Location tracks contract status (None/Active M2M/Active Term+expiration). New Opportunity/Contract-generation on an already-active Location auto-blocks, routes to human review.' Input contract: {locationIds: string[], companyId?: string (the Company this deal would belong to, if known - null/omitted for a brand-new lead that hasn't resolved a Company yet), opportunityId}. Meant to be called from TWO points: (1) advisory, non-blocking, right after lead-intake-to-demo-dashboard.workflow.json (W1.1) resolves/creates a Location, so a conflict surfaces early rather than only at payment time; (2) hard-blocking, right before stripe-payment-to-crm.workflow.json (W1.6) creates a new Contract, since that's the actual 'Contract-generation' moment the spec names.

nodes.name: Split locationIds
nodes.notes: Same Split Out + per-item fetch + single aggregating Code node pattern used throughout this library (e.g. hopper-load-campaign.workflow.json) rather than a filter query across multiple Location IDs, since Twenty CRM's REST filter support for an 'IN' style match isn't confirmed.

nodes.name: Fetch Location
nodes.notes: Runs once per split item, per n8n's default per-item execution for an HTTP Request node fed by Split Out - produces one output item per Location, all of which the next Code node receives together via $input.all() (Code node's default 'run once for all items' mode).

nodes.name: Evaluate lock conflicts
nodes.notes: The one piece of real decision logic in this workflow - everything else is plumbing around it. Deliberately returns amendmentCandidates even when not blocked, so a caller that gets 'allowed' back still knows whether it should be calling contract-amendment-flow.workflow.json instead of blindly creating a brand-new Contract (stripe-payment-to-crm.workflow.json's own 'new-logo path only' note flags exactly this gap).

nodes.name: Alert: Location Contract Lock conflict

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ severity: 'warning', source: 'location-contract-lock-check', message: 'Location Contract Lock conflict on Opportunity ' + $('Location lock check webhook').item.json.body.opportunityId + ': ' + $json.reason, linkUrl: ($env.TWENTY_CRM_BASE_URL || '') + '/objects/opportunity/' + $('Location lock check webhook').item.json.body.opportunityId }) }}

nodes.notes: 'Location Contract Lock conflict' is explicitly named as one of 05 Section 11's alert triggers - not an invented severity/routing choice. linkUrl (Command Center's primary-surface deep link, Step 3) points at a guessed Twenty CRM record URL pattern - unconfirmed, same REST-shape uncertainty as everything else, but a reasonable guess rather than omitting the link entirely.

nodes.name: Respond: blocked
nodes.notes: 409, not 403 - this isn't a permissions failure, it's a genuine state conflict (an already-active Contract) that a human resolving the conflict can clear, same conceptual shape as the dialer hopper's claim-race 409.
